title: Finite modules patch over a surjective ring fibre product
statement: Let $A'\twoheadrightarrow A$ be a surjective homomorphism of commutative rings, let $B\to A$ be a ring homomorphism, and put $I=\ker(A'\to A)$ and $R=B\times_A A'=\{(b,a'):b|_A=a'|_A\}$ with coordinatewise ring operations. Tensor products are those of [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product]. Let $N$ be a $B$-module, $M'$ an $A'$-module and $\varphi:N\otimes_B A\xrightarrow{\sim}M'/IM'$ an $A$-linear isomorphism. Put $M=M'/IM'$ and $P=N\times_M M'$, using $n\mapsto\varphi(n\otimes1)$, with the coordinatewise $R$-action. If $N$ is finitely generated over $B$ and $M'$ is finitely generated over $A'$, then $P$ is finitely generated over $R$ [def-weil-finitely-generated-module]. No flatness, nilpotence, Noetherian or finite-generation hypothesis on $I$ is imposed; zero rings and modules are allowed.

proof.text: Write $q:A'\twoheadrightarrow A$, $p:P\to N$ and $\rho:P\to M'$ for the maps in the statement. The map $R\to B$ is onto: given $b\in B$, lift its image in $A$ to $a'\in A'$, obtaining $(b,a')\in R$. Likewise $p$ is onto because every $\varphi(n\otimes1)\in M'/IM'$ has a representative in $M'$. Choose finite generating lists $y_1,\ldots,y_r$ of $N$ over $B$ and $x_1,\ldots,x_s$ of $M'$ over $A'$ using [def-weil-finitely-generated-module], and choose $u_i\in P$ with $p(u_i)=y_i$.

source.place: Tag 0D2H, proof, choice of generators and the lifts u_i; Situation 08KH

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-patched-module-base-change] to this same surjection $A'\to A$, ring map $B\to A$ and gluing isomorphism $\varphi$. Its second canonical isomorphism is $P\otimes_R A'\xrightarrow{\sim}M'$, $v\otimes a'\mapsto a'\rho(v)$. By the pure-tensor generation in [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product], each inverse image of $x_i$ is a finite sum of tensors $v\otimes a'$. Collect the finitely many first factors occurring for all $i$ into a list $v_1,\ldots,v_t\in P$. Their images $\rho(v_j)$ generate $M'$ over $A'$: each $x_i$ is a linear combination of them, and the $x_i$ generate. Thus no assertion that $P\to M'$ is surjective is needed.

source.place: Tag 0D2H, proof, finite tensor expressions for x_i; Tag 07RU, canonical A-prime base-change isomorphism

proof.text: Let $\xi\in P$. Write $p(\xi)=\sum_i b_i y_i$ and lift each $b_i\in B$ to $b'_i\in R$ using step 1. Then $\delta=\xi-\sum_i b'_iu_i$ has first coordinate zero. By the defining equality of $P=N\times_{M'/IM'}M'$, it has the form $(0,\theta)$ with $\theta\in IM'$. By definition of the product of an ideal and a module, write $\theta=\sum_{k=1}^{h}i_k m'_k$ with $i_k\in I$, and expand $m'_k=\sum_{j=1}^{t}a'_{kj}\rho(v_j)$ using step 2. Regrouping gives $\theta=\sum_j t_j\rho(v_j)$ where $t_j=\sum_k i_ka'_{kj}\in I$, since $I$ is an ideal.

source.place: Tag 0D2H, proof, subtraction of the lifted N-generators and expression of theta in IM-prime

proof.text: For each $j$ set $s_j=(0,t_j)\in R$; this is in $R$ because $q(t_j)=0$, and its first coordinate is zero. Coordinatewise scalar multiplication gives $\sum_j s_jv_j=(0,\sum_jt_j\rho(v_j))=(0,\theta)=\delta$. Consequently $\xi=\sum_i b'_iu_i+\sum_j s_jv_j$. The finite list $u_1,\ldots,u_r,v_1,\ldots,v_t$ therefore generates $P$ over $R$, which is finite generation by [def-weil-finitely-generated-module]. Empty lists and zero rings are admitted by the same equalities; no finiteness condition on $I$ was used.

source.place: Tag 0D2H, proof, kernel coefficients s_j and final generator formula
